samples.summary: Held render consumes the dirty-block set, so the replayed paint re-measures the WHOLE document on every keystroke
samples.evidence: The held branch calls `this.requestLayoutRefresh?.()` (text-editor.ts:739), wired to `recomputeLayout` (editor.ts:2531). `recomputeLayout` ends with `dirtyBlockIds = undefined` (editor.ts:1534). The replay at the end of `withUndoUnit` (text-editor.ts:3846-3848) then runs the host's real `render()` → `recomputeLayout()` a second time, now with `dirtyBlockIds === undefined`, and `computeLayout` sets `canUseCache = cache != null && dirtyBlockIds != null && …` (layout.ts:456-459) — i.e. undefined disables the incremental cache entirely and every block is re-measured. Concretely for typing: `handleInput` does `markDirty(blockId)` (line 1035) then `requestRender()` (line 1047) *inside* the unit, so the dirty set is consumed by the non-painting refresh and the final painting pass is a full-document layout. Before this change the single render consumed the dirty set and re-measured one block. This is on the hottest path (every character, Enter, paste) and defeats the incremental-layout invariant the package documents ("keeps arrow-key navigation O(1) instead of O(document)", editor.ts:2440-2444). Nothing in the suite counts layout passes — the new test only counts `ctx.save` paints — so CI will not catch it.

samples.summary: Folding a composite action into one Yorkie change makes redo restore the mid-action caret, not the final one
samples.evidence: `YorkieDocStore` records history presence only for the first write of a change: `consumePendingCursor()` nulls `pendingCursorPos` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:3175-3179) and every write only calls `recordHistoryPresence` when it got a non-null value (e.g. insertText, yorkie-doc-store.ts:1733-1737). Inside `withUndoUnit` the first write is now `deleteSelection()`'s delete, so the change's *post-edit* presence is the caret at the deletion point; every later write in the same batch records nothing, and the live cursor publish is suppressed while a batch is open (`skipNonHistoryPresence`, yorkie-doc-store.ts:3217). Yorkie re-applies the change's presence on redo, so Cmd+Shift+Z after typing/pasting over a selection should leave the caret at the delete position rather than after the inserted text. The reverse (undo) presence is still correct, so this is redo-only.

samples.summary: pastePlainTextFromClipboard's bare `catch {}` now swallows failures of the whole undo unit, including a Yorkie rollback
samples.evidence: The `withUndoUnit(...)` write block (lines 4256-4261) sits inside the same `try` whose `catch {}` is documented as being for "Clipboard API unavailable or permission denied" (line 4262-4264). A throw from `deleteSelection`/`insertPlainText` (e.g. `Block not found` from `findBlockInAnyArray`, memory.ts:503) is therefore silently discarded: on `YorkieDocStore` `batch()` rolls the whole `doc.update` back (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2940-2948), so the user's paste vanishes with no error anywhere. Every other paste path deliberately lets the throw reach `window.onerror` (see the comment at text-editor.ts:1592-1595).

samples.summary: After a rolled-back batch the editor's caret/selection still describe writes that never landed
samples.evidence: `withUndoUnit` runs `this.doc.batch(fn)` (line 3843) and, on a throw, `DocumentModel.batch` re-reads the store and rethrows (document.ts:146-153) while `YorkieDocStore.batch` discards the whole `doc.update`. But the view state mutated inside the body is not reverted: e.g. in `deleteSelectionImpl`'s full-selection branch the cursor is moved to a freshly created block id (`this.cursor.moveTo({ blockId: emptyBlock.id, offset: 0 })`, line 4056) — after a rollback that block does not exist, and the next keystroke's `this.doc.getBlock(this.cursor.position.blockId)` (line 976) throws `Block not found`. Previously the delete's writes survived the throw, so the caret stayed valid. Requires a prior exception inside the unit, so containment is the reason for the low severity, not doubt about the mechanism.

samples.summary: Undo floor now depends on SDK object identity; if an entry is ever rebuilt or copied the floor silently disappears and the initial load becomes undoable
samples.evidence: `canUndo()` resolves the floor with `stack.lastIndexOf(this.undoFloorMark)` and treats "not found" (-1) as "everything is above the floor". That is only sound while the *only* way an entry leaves the stack is FIFO eviction. If `getUndoStackForTest()` ever returns copied entries, or the SDK rebuilds/filters undo entries (e.g. on a remote change), the mark stops matching and the guard opens completely — the user can then undo the `writeFullDocument` load, which the comment at yorkie-doc-store.ts:614-618 says "would destroy blocks the cursor still references". The previous depth comparison was immune to identity. The existing test at packages/frontend/tests/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:344-357 pins identity for the pinned SDK version (0.7.19), so this is a latent fragility rather than a live bug.

samples.summary: The render hold is keyed on `undoUnitDepth`, not on the store's batch depth, so a `withUndoUnit` nested inside an external `doc.batch` would paint mid-transaction
samples.evidence: `requestRender` only defers while `this.undoUnitDepth > 0` (line 734-742) and `withUndoUnit` replays as soon as *its own* depth hits 0 (line 3846). A caller that opens `doc.batch(...)` directly and then reaches a `withUndoUnit` path (e.g. `deleteSelection`) would get `hostRequestRender()` called while the store's transaction is still open — painting a half-written batch, the exact thing the doc comment at line 3820-3827 promises cannot happen. No such caller exists today (`editor.ts:1238` `withNamedStyleChange` and `link-run.ts:105` only make style/store writes), so this is latent.

verdict.reason: Every element of the finding checks out in the working tree. text-editor.ts:734-743 shows the held-render branch calling `this.requestLayoutRefresh?.()` (739), which editor.ts:2531 binds to `recomputeLayout`. `recomputeLayout` passes `dirtyBlockIds` to `computeLayout` (editor.ts:1526) and then unconditionally clears it — `dirtyBlockIds = undefined` (editor.ts:1534) — with `markDirty` (editor.ts:1582-1587) the only repopulator. `computeLayout` gates the incremental cache on `dirtyBlockIds != null` (layout.ts:456-459, documented at 434-436), so `undefined` re-measures every block; editor.ts:1673-1676 confirms `dirtyBlockIds = undefined` is the deliberate "force full recompute" signal. `withUndoUnit` (text-editor.ts:3840-3851) decrements the depth before calling `this.requestRender()`, so the replay reaches `hostRequestRender` = `renderWithScroll` (editor.ts:2434-2438) -> `render()` (editor.ts:2208-2211) -> a second `recomputeLayout()` with the dirty set already consumed. The typing path is inside a unit and marks exactly one block dirty before requesting the render (text-editor.ts:1020-1048, markDirty at 1035, requestRender at 1038/1047), so the painting pass is a full-document layout on every keystroke/Enter/paste. Nothing re-marks dirty between the held refresh and the replay, so there is no guard; the state handoff breaks the incremental-layout invariant the package documents at editor.ts:2440-2444. This is an incorrect state update / broken invariant on a hot real path, within the correctness lane, so I cannot refute it on any named ground.
